title: POC Inception — Co‑creation Workshop Notes
context_and_objective: Summary: 2-day customer co-creation inception to align scope, success metrics, and a pragmatic deployment approach for a payments fraud detection POC. Objective: leave with a 6-week POC plan (milestones, responsibilities, infra footprint), an initial prompt/eval plan, and a signed statement of work stub. Customer: FinEdge (enterprise payments). Primary constraints: sensitive data, latency < 200ms 95th, budget cap for Dedicated capacity trial.
audience_and_participants: Redwood attendees: Solutions Eng lead, ML infra engineer, Product PM, SRE on-call (backup). Customer attendees: Head of Fraud, Eng manager (backend), Data scientist, Security architect, Platform ops. External: Channel partner (optional).
prework_for_customer:
- Provide sample telemetry and a 48-hour batch of non-PII request logs (anonymized).
- Confirm network constraints for VPC peering and egress rules.
- Identify 2 canonical fraud detection queries and 1 hard negative case.
- Assign an internal POC owner for approvals.
Note: Prework due 7 days before workshop.
logistics: Duration: two half-days (Day 1: 4 hours, Day 2: 3.5 hours). Location: customer HQ conference room + hybrid Zoom link. Materials: whiteboard, sticky notes, laptop for shared slides, sample dataset on secure S3 bucket, access to a test VPC. Recording permission requested from customer.
agenda_day_1:
1) 15m — Welcome, objectives, success criteria alignment.
2) 30m — Customer problem framing (deep dive from Head of Fraud).
3) 30m — Live data walkthrough (customer data scientist).
4) 20m — Quick demo: Redwood hosted flow for similar use case (15–20 tokens demo).
5) 40m — Breakout #1: Define 3 hypothesis-driven POC goals (teams: detection rate, latency/cost, integration coordinates).
6) 30m — Report back + prioritize goals (dot-vote).
7) 35m — Design session: minimal viable architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
8) 20m — Decision checkpoint: choose primary deployment path and fallback.
9) 10m — Q&A and homework (prep evaluation prompts and acceptance tests).
agenda_day_2:
1) 20m — Recap & alignment on chosen POC goal.
2) 45m — Implementation plan workshop: milestones, owners, infra tasks, security checklist.
3) 30m — Prompt/eval design: establish 8 seed prompts, success thresholds (Precision@N, FPR), and monitoring hooks.
4) 25m — Ops runbook sketch: deployment runbook, rollback plan, alert thresholds.
5) 20m — Customer integration plan: SDKs, webhook shapes, throughput expectations.
6) 20m — Risk table & mitigations (data sensitivity, model degradation, capacity limits).
7) 20m — Next steps, sign-offs, and timeline to SOW draft.
facilitator_notes_and_techniques:
- Start with a tight parking-lot for open questions and return to it daily.
- Use the hypothesis template: "When X happens, we expect Y change in metric Z".
- For breakout groups: give explicit roles (scribe, presenter, critic).
- Timebox tightly; use 5-minute warnings and a visible countdown.
- If technical blockers emerge, escalate to SRE lead after 10m of focused troubleshooting; don't let it derail agenda.
- Capture decisions as single-line artifacts prefixed with DECISION: and add owner.

breakout_exercises_prompts:
Breakout #1 prompt: pick one POC goal and draft an experiment to validate it in 2 weeks. Deliverable: one hypothesis, one simple test dataset, and a metric to watch.
Breakout #2 prompt: sketch the minimal integration pipeline for a webhook that sends flagged transactions to the customer backend. Deliverable: sequence diagram + sample payload.
Timebox each breakout to 30–40 minutes.
acceptance_criteria_and_metrics: Primary metric: Precision at top-N (N=50) > 0.85 on seed dataset. Secondary: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 200ms for single-request path. Cost cap: total inference spend < $6k in pilot window unless escalated. Operational: automated alerts for delta > 5% in Precision over a rolling week.
risk_register_and_mitigations:
- Data sensitivity: Use anonymized extracts, apply column redaction; prefer Private deployment if full raw data required.
- Latency shortfall: Pre-warm cache, reserve Dedicated pool, optimize batching profile.
- Model quality drift: schedule nightly evals, baseline prompts, and auto-rollback policy.
- Integration delays: provide SDK stub and Postman collection during week 1.
- Compliance reviews late: insert legal review gate at milestone 2 and add 3 business days buffer.
action_items_and_owners:
- Redwood: prepare minimal infra spec and rough cost estimate (Avery) — due 3 business days.
- Customer: provide anonymized 48-hour logs + answer network questions (FinEdge eng lead) — due 7 days.
- Redwood ML: draft 8 seed prompts and 2 hard-negative examples for evaluation (Mariana) — due 5 days.
- SRE: validate VPC peering checklist and outbound rules (Samir) — due 4 days.
- Product: create SOW skeleton for 6-week POC (Jordan) — due 6 business days.
post_workshop_follow_up_template:
Email subject: 'POC Inception recap & next steps — FinEdge'
Body: 1) Thank you + attendees list. 2) Decisions made (bulleted). 3) Action items with owners and dates. 4) Attached: slide deck, architecture sketch, evaluation plan, SOW draft link.
Request: capture sign-off on POC goal and chosen deployment by COB +5 business days.
notes_and_open_questions:
- Confirm whether FinEdge requires HSM-backed KMS for keys in pilot.
- Clarify expected 99th percentile SLA if customer intends to go multi-region.
- Decide whether to include a model-interpretability deliverable in pilot scope.
- Customer to confirm which internal teams need view-only access to monitoring dashboards.
